content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through common attribute and value errors with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns reading stale or unexpected values into a repeatable implementation choice. Attributes describe markup; properties represent current DOM state. For example, checked and selected are runtime properties, while data-* attributes are markup strings and jQuery data values are a separate cache.

The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.

If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: Sets the image alternative text and loading attribute. Keep the alt text accurate for the actual image.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
